items.title: Preserve the exact product identity
items.content: WHEN: Planning or reviewing any product image or video. DO: Use the selected Shopify Product and Variant media as product truth. Preserve the visible silhouette, structure, finish, material appearance, proportions, and identifying details. DO NOT: Add, remove, or relocate visible product parts. If a surface or structure is not shown by a source, treat it as unknown rather than verified.
non_conclusions: A plausible unseen surface is not official product truth.

items.title: Describe the customer situation, not a stereotype
items.content: WHEN: A Creative Persona is needed. DO: Describe one concrete customer situation using the problem, desired change, buying trigger, objection, and useful proof. DO NOT: Invent demographics, customer research, or performance facts. EXAMPLE: Prefer 'a shopper trying to organize a crowded TV area' over 'women aged 25-35'.
non_conclusions: A newly inferred persona is a Creative hypothesis, not verified customer research.

items.title: Link verified features to supportable benefits
items.content: WHEN: Writing a Creative argument or choosing a visual demonstration. DO: Start with a feature verified by the selected product sources, state how the customer uses it, and describe only the resulting benefit that the evidence supports. Show only that supported benefit. DO NOT: Use generated water, impact, heat, or load scenes as proof of an unverified claim.
non_conclusions: Generated water, impact or heat demonstrations do not establish product claims.

items.title: Keep concept, hook, and format separate
items.content: WHEN: Defining a Creative direction. DO: Define the concept as the customer situation and product argument; define the hook as what the viewer sees or hears first; define the format as the image or video treatment. DO NOT: Use a format label such as 'lifestyle video' as the complete concept. An offer is optional and requires current support.
non_conclusions: An offer is optional and must be current and supported.

items.title: Make the opening and payoff tell one story
items.content: WHEN: Writing a hook, storyboard, or scene plan. DO: Make the opening establish the same situation or promise that the later product benefit resolves. DO NOT: Introduce one problem and then abandon it for unrelated beauty shots. Product-first and problem-first openings are both acceptable when the payoff stays coherent.
non_conclusions: Product-first and problem-first openings are both valid when coherent.

items.title: Assign one clear role to each image
items.content: WHEN: Planning more than one image for the same Variant. DO: Keep product truth and shared direction consistent, then give every image a distinct job such as hero, room context, supported feature, detail, or use situation. DO NOT: Return near-duplicate compositions or treat example image counts as quotas.
non_conclusions: Template layout families and output counts are optional, not quotas.

items.title: Give every video shot a purpose
items.content: WHEN: Planning a video. DO: Assign each shot one explicit purpose such as context, problem, function, detail, proof, transition, or final hero; then choose framing and motion that serve that purpose. DO NOT: Add motion only for visual activity or impose a fixed shot count.
non_conclusions: This does not ban dynamic motion or impose a shot count.

items.title: Check continuity across shots and modalities
items.content: WHEN: Planning or reviewing a multi-shot or multimodal Creative. DO: Keep product geometry, color, scale, room layout, recurring people, text, and spoken message consistent from one shot to the next. DO NOT: Let a new camera angle invent product geometry that no approved source shows.
non_conclusions: A new camera angle does not prove unseen product geometry.

items.title: Prepare a simpler product base only when necessary
items.content: WHEN: An authorized generative route cannot reliably place a complex product from the available source views. DO: Consider a simpler reviewed candidate base before adding room context or complex motion. DO NOT: Treat that generated base as product evidence or redraw a product on an exact-source route.
non_conclusions: A generated base is not product evidence and exact-source routes must not redraw products.

items.title: Revise the smallest meaningful part
items.content: WHEN: Human feedback requests another version. DO: State which accepted elements must remain unchanged, identify the smallest image, shot, copy, or concept component that must change, and revise only that component when the tools allow it. DO NOT: Restart unrelated parts or assume unlimited paid retries.
non_conclusions: This does not authorize unlimited paid retries.

items.title: Make every variation test one deliberate difference
items.content: WHEN: Producing multiple variations. DO: State what each variation changes, why that change matters, and which unrelated elements should remain stable. DO NOT: Create variations that differ only by vague wording or copy historical output counts as universal rules.
non_conclusions: Historical angle, hook, image and job counts are not global quotas.

items.title: Do not confuse Creative approval with Ads performance
items.content: WHEN: Interpreting a review or performance claim. DO: Treat human approval as acceptance of one exact Creative version. Require exact asset-to-ad lineage, metric window, objective, attribution basis, and known confounds before describing Ads effectiveness. DO NOT: Call an asset a winner from CTR alone, a folder-level result, or one anomalous conversion.
non_conclusions: CTR, folder-level outcomes or one anomalous conversion do not prove a winning asset.

items.title: Transfer Creative patterns, never another SKU's facts
items.content: WHEN: Reusing a reference, lesson, or previous Creative from another SKU. DO: Transfer only an applicable situation, hook mechanism, composition, or production technique. Rebuild product facts, offers, claims, prices, and testimonials from the selected SKU's approved sources. DO NOT: Copy factual statements merely because the previous product looks similar.
non_conclusions: An exact SKU match in historical Creative is not required to create a grounded new concept.

items.title: Honor human settings and current provider capabilities
items.content: WHEN: Preparing or executing an output plan. DO: Treat the human-selected text mode, duration, output profile, and verified active-model capabilities as binding constraints. Use historical documents only as Creative guidance. DO NOT: Override current settings with old durations, overlay lengths, logo practices, provider names, or capabilities.
non_conclusions: Historical overlay lengths, durations, logo use and provider names are not current capability facts.

items.title: Apply local feedback locally before proposing a reusable lesson
items.content: WHEN: Human feedback is recorded for an output. DO: Apply the exact comment to the current revision within its pinned product and media scope. If the idea may be reusable, create a separate lesson proposal with sources, scope, limits, and counterexamples for human review. DO NOT: Turn one preference or positive review into a team rule or performance fact.
non_conclusions: A local preference or positive review does not automatically become a team rule or performance fact.

items.title: SOP: Assemble only relevant Creative context
items.content: WHEN: Preparing context for one SKU. DO: Start with the exact selected Product or Variant and the human request; then add only approved brand, category, historical, and feedback knowledge whose scope matches. Preserve every source reference and uncertainty. DO NOT: Import unrelated product facts or require a live Lark lookup to complete the run.
non_conclusions: Lark is not a required runtime dependency and no fixed keyword fallback ladder is prescribed.

items.title: SOP: Write an executable image brief
items.content: WHEN: Preparing an image output. DO: Specify the image's role, composition, focal hierarchy, product position and scale, viewpoint, setting, lighting, palette, human presence, approved text and logo treatment, product locks, and negative constraints. DO NOT: Leave another strategy-writing step for production or copy facts from an old template.
non_conclusions: This SOP does not require a fixed image count, text layer or provider.

items.title: SOP: Write a duration-aware video plan
items.content: WHEN: Preparing a video output. DO: Define one coherent promise, give every shot a purpose, preserve continuity, and make scene durations add up to the requested final duration within verified model limits. Use multiple source clips only when the final duration exceeds one supported source duration, and specify transitions and trims. DO NOT: Assume every provider supports every duration or assembly feature.
non_conclusions: The Dashboard's 1-30 second requirement does not prove that every provider supports every duration or assembly feature.

items.title: SOP: Give every reference one explicit role
items.content: WHEN: Selecting or applying references. DO: Label Shopify media as product truth, Research media as mood or execution inspiration, and previous outputs as review history. Use Research only for applicable layout, framing, lighting, palette, or Creative pattern. DO NOT: Copy a reference's product, logo, advertiser, text, offer, or claim into the selected SKU.
non_conclusions: A candidate base does not establish missing product geometry.

items.title: SOP: Review fidelity, message, and requested settings
items.content: WHEN: A human reviews an image or video. DO: Check exact product fidelity, supported function, message clarity, and compliance with requested settings. Record what passes, what fails, and the smallest meaningful correction. DO NOT: Treat Creative acceptance as Ads activation, performance proof, or approval of a reusable team rule.
non_conclusions: Creative acceptance is separate from Ads activation and team-rule promotion.

items.title: SOP: Turn feedback into a reviewable lesson proposal
items.content: WHEN: A human chooses to generalize feedback. DO: Preserve the exact observation, separate observed facts from inferred causes, define where the lesson applies, compare it with existing knowledge, and include limits or counterexamples. Publish it only as a proposal until a human approves that exact version. DO NOT: Use metadata alone as proof that the lesson is broadly valid.
non_conclusions: Metadata supports audit and scope; it does not replace LLM orchestration with keyword rules.

items.title: Show rest, not treatment
items.content: WHEN: Planning AuraSleep images or video. DO: Show the product in use early, in a calm, softly lit bedroom, with a relaxed person who looks rested. Keep the light-grey knit pillow and dusk-blue blanket colors exact. DO NOT: Frame people as patients, show pain, or imply the product cures or treats a condition.
non_conclusions: Comfort claims stay experiential, not medical.

items.title: Let the wood carry the story
items.content: WHEN: Planning OaklineHome images or video. DO: Use bright daylight interiors with one or two props, keep real wood grain visible and proportions believable for a small home, and show one everyday use per shot. DO NOT: Clutter the room, change the finish, or show the furniture at an impossible scale.
non_conclusions: Room styling is inspiration, not part of the product.

items.title: Describe the feel, never the result
items.content: WHEN: Planning LumiSkin images or video. DO: Use bright diffused light, glass and water textures, and natural skin with visible texture; show the frosted bottle or tube exactly as packshot. DO NOT: Promise results, show before/after comparisons, or retouch skin into plastic perfection.
non_conclusions: Skin appearance in an ad is not evidence of product efficacy.

items.title: Hook early and show the product in the first frames
items.content: WHEN: Planning any short vertical video ad. DO: Put the hook and the product in the first 3 seconds, state the main benefit or offer within about 6 seconds, and keep one idea per shot. DO NOT: Open on a logo card, a slow fade, or a scene without the product.
non_conclusions: Timing guidance is a starting point, not a guarantee of performance.

items.title: Respect vertical format and safe zones
items.content: WHEN: Planning or reviewing 9:16 video or story-format images. DO: Compose for 9:16 at 720p or higher and keep faces, the product, and any text away from the top and bottom edges where platform interface elements cover the frame. DO NOT: Place the call to action or key text in the bottom strip.
non_conclusions: Exact safe-zone pixel sizes vary by placement and are not stated here.

items.title: Keep on-screen text short
items.content: WHEN: Writing captions or text overlays for video. DO: Use short lines that can be read at a glance, roughly no more than 10 words per second of screen time, and match the text to the spoken or visual beat. DO NOT: Stack paragraphs of copy or repeat the same message in three places.
non_conclusions: The word limit is a readability guide, not a platform rule.

items.title: Make the ad work with sound and without it
items.content: WHEN: Planning video audio and captions. DO: Treat sound as part of the ad because most Reels views play with sound on, and still make the story understandable when muted by using clear visuals and brief captions. DO NOT: Rely on voice-over alone to explain what the product is.
non_conclusions: Share of sound-on views differs by placement and audience.

items.title: Show the brand early and keep it present
items.content: WHEN: Planning any ad. DO: Make the product and brand identifiable in the opening, keep them visible or referenced through the ad, feature a real person using the product where it fits the brand, and end on one clear call to action. DO NOT: Save the product reveal for the last second.
non_conclusions: Lift figures from the source are platform-reported, not guaranteed.

items.title: Check text contrast and legibility
items.content: WHEN: Reviewing any image or video frame with text. CHECK: Normal text has at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background and large text at least 3:1, text sits inside safe margins, and nothing overlaps the product. FAIL IF: Text is hard to read on a busy background or is cropped by the format.
non_conclusions: Contrast ratios are a minimum accessibility bar, not a design quality score.

items.title: Choose the target group from the store's own numbers
items.content: WHEN: Resolving the persona for a product that has customer_segments data. DO: Pick the group with the largest share of this product's revenue or the clearest headroom (large store value, low penetration of this product), describe it from its size, repeat behavior, age and region mix and what it also buys, and cite the customer_segments source. DO NOT: Invent demographics, motives, or purchase intent that the numbers do not show.
non_conclusions: Segments describe past purchases and do not prove why people bought.

items.title: Match message and offer to the customer group
items.content: WHEN: Writing an angle for a chosen customer group. DO: Champions and Loyal customers get early access, new arrivals, or a thank-you, not a discount. Recent customers get complementary products and how-to-use content. Promising customers get social proof and a reason to buy again. Needs attention and At risk customers get a reminder of what they loved and a time-limited incentive only if a real code exists. Inactive customers and new prospects get a simple introduction and a reason to try. DO NOT: Speak as if you know a person's age, health, or finances.
non_conclusions: The mapping is a default hypothesis to test, not a proven result.

items.title: Give each target group its own concept
items.content: WHEN: Producing more than one variation for different customer groups. DO: Make each variation a different concept, setting, or format built for one group, so the ads differ in more than wording. DO NOT: Produce near-identical ads with only a swapped headline.
non_conclusions: Meta describes creative diversity as helpful; it does not publish a required number of ads.

items.title: Never imply you know personal attributes
items.content: WHEN: Writing copy or choosing a persona for any ad. DO: Speak to the situation, such as needs, moments, and benefits. DO NOT: Address the viewer with their age, health condition, body, finances, or other personal attributes, for example asking whether they suffer from a condition.
non_conclusions: This summarizes the intent of the personal attributes policy; read the current platform policy for exact wording.

items.title: A campaign theme changes the scene, not the facts
items.content: WHEN: A campaign theme such as Halloween, Tết, or Black Friday is requested. DO: Apply the theme to setting, props, mood, palette, and the tone of the copy while the real product stays the hero. Order of authority is brand rules and legal claims, then exact product truth, then the chosen customer group, then the theme, then style. DO NOT: Change product color, shape, price, claims, or brand identity to fit the theme.
non_conclusions: A theme is creative direction, not evidence that the product suits the occasion.

items.title: Handle cultural and religious occasions respectfully
items.content: WHEN: A theme refers to a cultural or religious occasion. DO: Use widely recognized, positive symbols and colors for that occasion, keep the tone respectful, and avoid anything that could read as mocking or sacred. DO NOT: Use sacred symbols as decoration or stereotype a culture.
non_conclusions: This is a team default, not a cultural authority; the team checks local meaning before publishing.

items.title: Claim only what the product data supports
items.content: WHEN: Writing any benefit, performance, or result statement. DO: Use only approved claims and facts present in the Shopify product data or brand guideline, and phrase comfort or feel as experience. DO NOT: Add health, safety, or result claims, rely on words like may or helps to soften a claim the data does not support, or imply testing that the data does not show.
non_conclusions: Advertising law varies by country; this rule is a conservative team default.

items.title: Use only real offers
items.content: WHEN: An ad mentions a price, discount, or deadline. DO: Use a price or code that exists in the store data and state the real conditions. DO NOT: Invent a sale, fake urgency, or a countdown that the store is not running.
non_conclusions: The presence of a discount code in the data does not mean it should be promoted.

items.title: Read fatigue from the ad's own decay
items.content: WHEN: Deciding whether an ad needs a refresh. DO: Compare click-through in the first and last 14 days and treat a drop of about 40 percent or more as a fatigue signal worth a new concept. Treat frequency above 3 or a two-to-three-week refresh cycle only as rough folklore. DO NOT: Retire a winning ad on frequency alone.
non_conclusions: No official platform threshold exists for ad fatigue.
The 40 percent figure is a team default.

items.title: Borrow patterns from references, not assets
items.content: WHEN: Using a research reference. DO: Describe what is borrowed as a pattern, such as hook type, shot structure, pacing, framing, or palette, and name that pattern in the plan. DO NOT: Copy another brand's logo, copy, claims, product, or recognizable people.
non_conclusions: A reference with a long run in the ad library may not have performed well; running time is only a proxy.

items.title: Anchor video scenes on a locked keyframe
items.content: WHEN: Planning a multi-scene video built from keyframes. DO: Create each scene's keyframe from the exact product media, describe only motion and camera movement for the animation, keep the same lighting, palette, and product look across scenes, and keep each scene to 15 seconds or less. DO NOT: Ask the animation step to redesign the product or add text.
non_conclusions: Keyframe-first planning reduces but does not remove product drift.

items.title: Shape the story to the video length
items.content: WHEN: Choosing scenes for a video of 15 to 60 seconds. DO: Use one idea for 15 seconds, hook then product in use then call to action for about 30 seconds, and add a proof or second use moment for 45 to 60 seconds. DO NOT: Stretch a 15-second idea over a longer video with filler.
non_conclusions: Structures are defaults; the brief may justify a different shape.

items.title: AuraSleep voice: calm, warm, reassuring
items.content: WHEN: Writing any AuraSleep copy or voice-over. DO: Use short, soft sentences about how mornings feel, for example waking up easy. DO NOT: Sound clinical, alarmist, or salesy; avoid words like cure, treat, relieve, or doctor.
non_conclusions: Voice rules are for the fictional demo brand.

items.title: AuraSleep look: soft morning light
items.content: WHEN: Planning AuraSleep visuals. DO: Use cloud white, light grey, and muted dusk blue, soft morning window light, tidy minimal bedrooms, and natural linen textures. DO NOT: Use harsh flash, neon accents, or cluttered rooms.
non_conclusions: Palette names describe the demo brand, not a trademark.

items.title: AuraSleep product depiction
items.content: WHEN: Showing an AuraSleep product. DO: Keep the pillow's butterfly contour and light-grey knit cover, the blanket's dusk-blue cotton cover and stitched pockets, the sheets' percale finish in cloud white or dusk blue, and the sleep mask's silk sheen exactly as in the packshot. DO NOT: Change colors, add patterns, or show features the packshot does not show.
non_conclusions: Material descriptions come from the product data.

items.title: AuraSleep claims: comfort, never treatment
items.content: WHEN: AuraSleep copy mentions sleep or body comfort. DO: Say how the product feels and fits, and mention the 100-night trial only for the pillow where the product data lists it. DO NOT: Claim to cure pain, act as a medical device, or be doctor recommended.
non_conclusions: Comfort language is experiential, not medical.

items.title: Oakline Home voice: confident and understated
items.content: WHEN: Writing any Oakline Home copy. DO: Talk about materials, craft, and everyday use in plain, confident sentences. DO NOT: Use superlatives like best or cheapest, or promise a lifetime guarantee.
non_conclusions: Voice rules are for the fictional demo brand.

items.title: Oakline Home look: daylight Scandinavian interiors
items.content: WHEN: Planning Oakline Home visuals. DO: Use walnut, natural oak, matte black, and warm white, daylight rooms with one plant or book as props, and eye-level or three-quarter angles. DO NOT: Use cluttered rooms, heavy filters, or dark moody lighting.
non_conclusions: Styling is inspiration, not part of the product.

items.title: Oakline Home product depiction and scale
items.content: WHEN: Showing Oakline furniture. DO: Keep the real wood grain, finish, proportions, and frame color from the packshot, such as the desk's black frame, the chair's rounded oak arms, the five-tier bookshelf with a matte black steel frame, and the round side table with tapered legs, and place each at a believable scale in a small home. DO NOT: Change finish or color, resize the piece to look bigger, or add features such as drawers.
non_conclusions: Dimensions come from the product data; unlisted sizes are unknown.

items.title: Oakline Home claims: only what the data lists
items.content: WHEN: Oakline copy describes build or materials. DO: Name solid wood, motors, presets, or finishes only when the product data lists them for that item. DO NOT: Claim lifetime guarantees, the lowest price, or a feature that is on a different product.
non_conclusions: A feature on one SKU is not proof for another.

items.title: LumiSkin voice: fresh, honest, gentle
items.content: WHEN: Writing any LumiSkin copy or voice-over. DO: Describe how skin feels, such as soft, comfortable, and hydrated-looking, in short, friendly sentences. DO NOT: Promise results, use fear or insecurity as a hook, or compare skin before and after.
non_conclusions: Voice rules are for the fictional demo brand.

items.title: LumiSkin look: bright, glassy, natural skin
items.content: WHEN: Planning LumiSkin visuals. DO: Use white, blush pink, and pale aqua, bright diffused light, glass and water textures, and dewy skin with visible texture. DO NOT: Retouch skin into plastic perfection or use heavy glamour lighting.
non_conclusions: Retouching limits are a brand choice, not a legal requirement.

items.title: LumiSkin product depiction
items.content: WHEN: Showing a LumiSkin product. DO: Keep each package exactly as in the packshot, such as the serum's frosted glass bottle with a white dropper, the sunscreen tube, the cleanser's frosted pump bottle, and the cream's airless pump. DO NOT: Turn a tube into a bottle, invent label text or logos, or change the cap or dropper color.
non_conclusions: Generated images can add text; reviewers check labels against the packshot.

items.title: LumiSkin claims: appearance and feel only
items.content: WHEN: LumiSkin copy describes skin or sun protection. DO: Keep to appearance and feel, such as hydrated-looking or comfortable, and state SPF 50 broad-spectrum only for the sunscreen where the data lists it. DO NOT: Claim to treat acne or conditions, remove wrinkles, or be clinically proven, and never imply one application protects all day.
non_conclusions: Claims that treat or prevent a condition can make a product a drug under US rules.
Rules for other countries were not reviewed.
